answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring every agent to lock a refundable stake that is slashed when fraud is proven, so each fake identity costs real money. Like a raven watching a canyon pass, reputation must be earned through verified work over time, while a lantern of public on-chain history exposes copycats at once. An attacker must therefore fund many stakes and fake long histories, making the attack far more expensive than anything it could steal.
